Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Birth registration completeness 54% (2018); ~62% recent estimates; proxy for coverage.
revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched and verified. World Bank data (compiled from UNICEF-collated DHS/MICS household surveys) confirms birth registration completeness at 61.9% for Cameroon in 2018, the most recent data point published; UNICEF's CRVS country profile is dated 2017 with its next update pending. No more recent nationally representative completeness survey was found. Birth registration completeness is the standard proxy for civil register coverage, and 61.9% sits within the 50-69% band, confirming the existing score.
revised_comments: Cameroon's civil register (CRVS) coverage is measured using birth registration completeness as the standard proxy, most recently estimated at 61.9% (2018 DHS/MICS-based data compiled by UNICEF and reported via the World Bank). This places coverage within the 50-69% band. Legislative reforms from 2024 have introduced electronic declaration of civil status acts, a national civil status database and electronic certificates, indicating ongoing modernisation of the underlying system, though no more recent nationally representative completeness survey has been published to update the coverage estimate.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital electoral register?
Comments: Digital biometric electoral register by ELECAM since 2013; updated annually; 13th-gen kits 2025.
revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched and verified. The ACE Electoral Knowledge Network case study, authored by an Elections Cameroon (ELECAM) official, confirms nationwide biometric voter registration (BVR) was implemented in 2012-2013. ELECAM's official portal, currently live, confirms the register remains active and continuously maintained, with ongoing revision of electoral rolls via council branches and mobile teams and an online enrolment-verification service. This supports the maximum score of 5 (Fully deployed nationwide). Because this is a top-of-scale score, it is flagged for human review per policy even though the evidence is authoritative and current.
revised_comments: Cameroon's electoral register has been digital and biometric since Elections Cameroon (ELECAM) implemented biometric voter registration nationwide in 2012-2013. The system remains fully operational and continuously maintained: ELECAM's portal shows ongoing revision of electoral registers through council branches and mobile registration teams, an online enrolment-verification service, and periodic equipment upgrades (13th-generation registration kits referenced for 2025), indicating a fully deployed, nationwide, continuously updated biometric voter register.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more social protection registers?
Comments: CNPS digital registration tele-registration; RESUC unified social registry mentioned with interoperability plans.
revision_notes: The originally cited sources (a CNPS online-registration announcement and a 21-country World Bank digital social protection overview) mainly evidence a separate contributory social-security registration channel and a general diagnostic-stage reference to Cameroon, rather than direct evidence of social protection registry deployment. Fresh searches identified stronger, more specific and more current evidence: Cameroon's Ministry of Social Affairs operates a Unified Social Registry (Registre Social Unifie du Cameroun, RESUC) for socially vulnerable persons, with a national rollout launched in August 2024 across 100 pilot social centres in all ten regions (targeting 250,000 households by June 2025) and continuing regional expansion reported into 2026 (e.g. West Region: circa 55,000 people enrolled across a growing number of communes as of April 2026, locally described as still a low uptake rate). This is consistent with an operational but not yet nationwide register, confirming the existing score of 4 (Partially deployed).
revised_comments: Cameroon's Ministry of Social Affairs operates a Unified Social Registry (Registre Social Unifie du Cameroun, RESUC), a beneficiary and vulnerability database supported by the World Bank, UNICEF and the World Food Programme. Following a pilot phase, national rollout began in August 2024 with 100 social centres equipped across all ten regions, targeting registration of 250,000 vulnerable households by mid-2025. Regional deployment continues through 2026, with enrolment expanding commune by commune (for example around 55,000 people registered across a growing number of communes in the West Region by April 2026), though uptake remains uneven and coverage is not yet nationwide. Cameroon separately operates a CNPS-managed digital registration channel for contributory social security.
